source.title: Online Learning: A Modern Introduction Using Convex Optimization
source.anchor: Lemma 6.33, printed p. 80; Definition 6.4, Eq. (6.4) and Example 6.6, printed pp. 63–64; the proof of Theorem 13.4, printed pp. 210–211.

target: Prove the modulus-one chord and support bounds on the positive weighted simplex. Relate the entropy Bregman divergence to finite KL, retain the mass correction, and extend the binary estimate to both endpoints with a fair reference.

searched_existing: The weighted ambient entropy derivative and normalized pairing, convex-carrier equivalence, feasible affine support growth, PiLp with exponent 1, and the existing binary KL definition.
known_consumers: The interior KL lower bound uses the entropy support estimate. The closed fair-coin bound and its scaled form use the same two-coordinate KL specialization.
The public canaries specialize the modulus-one chord bound and two distinct feasible supporting functionals.
planned_consumers: The continuous-coin wealth bound also needs its gamma-potential and endpoint recurrence arguments.
reuse_plan.decision_reason: The actual ℓ¹ norm on PiLp 1 gives the squared distance in both strong-convexity inequalities. The KL identity keeps the linear mass correction until both vectors have total mass one. The Bernoulli formula extends continuously in its first argument with the second argument fixed at 1/2.

semantic_roundtrip.remaining_semantic_delta: The weighted comparison set contains exactly positive weight-normalized vectors. Generalized KL admits zero numerators and requires strictly positive reference coordinates. The closed Bernoulli result fixes the reference probability at 1/2.
